source_work: Noah Webster, An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828)
rights_basis: The original 1828 dictionary text is public domain; only its historical definitions and examples are transcribed, not website editorial material.
transcription_source: Internet Archive volume 2 printed page scans and OCR, cross-checked against clean online Webster transcriptions; original OCR is retained unchanged.
selection_method: Selected the next four exact KJV-used S headwords in alphabetical order from the unreviewed high/medium OCR queue. This is a targeted OCR queue, not a claim that all Webster entries have been reviewed.
review_method: Visually checked every sense against the printed page scans and used clean online transcriptions only as secondary aids. Corrected OCR substitutions, scan breaks, page headers, punctuation, and numbering; retained historical examples, usage labels, and author citations. Expanded parts of speech and normalized whitespace for display. Source spans are one-based lines in the hash-verified OCR file.
review_scope: All definitions and examples: two STING transitive senses and five noun senses; six STOMACH noun senses, two transitive senses, and its intransitive definition; three STOOL noun senses, stool of repentance, and its intransitive definition; six STORY noun senses and two transitive senses. Readable etymology is retained while uncertain non-Latin characters are conservatively transliterated rather than guessed.
